name: Muhammad
gender_note: Recorded as an Arabic male given name.
primary_meaning: Muhammad (Arabic مُحَمَّد, Muḥammad) is an Arabic male given name meaning “praiseworthy” or “praised”. It is the name of the Prophet of Islam, and is believed to be the most common given name in the world.
literal_meaning: Praised, praiseworthy (passive participle of ḥammada, “to praise”)
meaning_explanation: The name is the passive participle of the Arabic verb ḥammada (حَمَّدَ), “to praise”, from the Semitic root Ḥ-M-D. A passive participle names the one who receives the action, so the sense is “the one who is praised” — hence “praiseworthy”. Other Arabic names built on the same root include Ahmad, Mahmud, Hamid and Tahmid.

etymology.morphology: Passive participle (mufaʿʿal pattern) of the form-II verb ḥammada, “to praise”.
etymology.explanation: From the passive participle of ḥammada (حَمَّدَ), “to praise”, on the triconsonantal Semitic root Ḥ-M-D.

origin.explanation: Arabic in origin. It spread wherever Islam spread, producing many local forms — Mehmet/Mehmed in Turkish, Mamadou in West Africa, Magomed in the Caucasus, Maxamed in Somali.

religion.association: Islamic — name of the Prophet Muhammad
religion.status: Name of the Prophet of Islam; occurs in the Qur'an
religion.explanation: Muhammad is the name of the Prophet of Islam, and the name itself occurs in the Qur'an (for example Surah Muhammad, 47:2). Muslim families give it in his honour, often as the first element of a compound name.

quranic.note: The name Muhammad occurs four times in the Qur'an.

naming_context.context: Given across the Muslim world in honour of the Prophet; in South Asia it is often written in shortened form (Md., Mohd.) before a second name.
naming_context.interpretation: Chosen first of all for its association with the Prophet, and secondly for its meaning, “praised”.
naming_context.important_distinction: The meaning “praised” comes from Arabic grammar; the name's religious weight comes from the Prophet who bore it.

cultural.meaning: Its popularity is so broad that the name has one of the largest numbers of English spelling variants in the world.
cultural.impact: The Independent reported in 2014 that more than 150 million men and boys bear the name, which would make it the most popular name in the world.

items: Arabic passive participle used as a personal name; borne by the Prophet Muhammad in 7th-century Mecca and Medina.
Spread with Islam into Turkish (Mehmed), Persian, Urdu, African and Caucasian naming traditions.
history.person: The Prophet Muhammad (c. 570–632), founder of Islam.

modern_usage: Usually listed as the most common given name in the world when its spellings are counted together; the name has been banned for newborns in China's Xinjiang region since 2017.

pronunciation.note: Egyptian Arabic says [mæˈħæmːæd]; the double m is held. Urdu and Persian speakers use a plain h.

variant_notes: Mehmet/Mehmed are the Turkish forms, Mamadou is common in West Africa, Magomed in the North Caucasus and Maxamed in Somali.

faq.a: Muhammad is Arabic for “praised” or “praiseworthy”. It is the passive participle of ḥammada, “to praise”.
Yes. The name Muhammad occurs four times in the Qur'an (3:144, 33:40, 47:2 and 48:29), and Surah 47 is named after him.

faq.q: What is the root of Muhammad?
faq.a: The triconsonantal root Ḥ-M-D (ح م د), “praise”. Ahmad, Mahmud and Hamid share the same root.

faq.q: How many people are named Muhammad?
faq.a: The Independent reported in 2014 that more than 150 million men and boys bear the name, which would make it the most popular given name in the world.

faq.q: What are other spellings of Muhammad?
faq.a: Mohammed, Mohammad, Muhammed, Mohamed, Mehmet (Turkish), Mamadou (West Africa), Magomed (Caucasus) and many more.
moo-HAM-mad, with a breathy Arabic ḥ and a doubled m: /muˈħammad/.

faq.q: What does Md. or Mohd. mean before a name?
faq.a: They are common written abbreviations of Muhammad, especially in South Asia and Malaysia.
